name: patient-cohort
title: Hemorrhage across the shipped patients
question:
Does the same right-leg hemorrhage (severity 0.8, 10 minutes) produce the
same qualitative response in all 21 patients that ship with Pulse, and how
does the fraction of blood lost depend on the patient's starting blood volume?
hypothesis: Every patient loses blood volume, raises heart rate and loses arterial pressure. Absolute blood loss varies much less than starting blood volume does, so patients with a smaller starting blood volume lose a larger fraction of it.
objective:
Run pulse_hemorrhage (RightLeg, severity 0.8, 600 s) once from each of the 21
stabilized states in Pulse's install (bin/states/*@0s.json) and compare the
final vitals and the fraction of blood lost.

readouts.name: irreversible-state
readouts.description: Pulse reported an irreversible state; the engine is no longer advanced.

units_and_time.note: Pulse's own clock; its internal solver step is 0.02 s.

expected_behavior.name: every-patient-compensates
expected_behavior.condition: in all 21 patients blood volume and MAP fall and heart rate rises

expected_behavior.name: smaller-patients-lose-larger-fraction
expected_behavior.condition: Spearman rank correlation with starting blood volume <= -0.7

comparative_visualizations.name: map-by-patient
comparative_visualizations.title: MAP during the same bleed in every shipped patient

robustness.note: Pulse is deterministic; the cohort is a sweep over the patient state file.

predictions: Pilot probe (direct pulse_hemorrhage runs, 600 s): all 21 states load; fraction lost ranges 23.8% (Overweight) to 38.1% (Underweight); Spearman rank correlation of fraction lost with starting blood volume is -0.91.
preregistered.thresholds_provenance: The -0.7 correlation threshold is set below that pilot value; the qualitative criteria follow from the hypothesis.
preregistered.pilot: Criteria were written after a direct pilot of the same 21 configurations (workspace/experiments/_runs.yaml, pilot-2026-10-23-patients), which gave Spearman rho = -0.91. Pulse is deterministic, so these criteria are regression checks on the canonical runs, not out-of-sample predictions.

falsifiability:
Refuted if any patient fails to load or run, if any patient's blood volume,
heart rate or MAP moves the other way, or if the rank correlation of fraction
lost with starting blood volume is above -0.7.
limitations: The 21 patients are Pulse's shipped examples, not a population sample.
The same severity number does not mean the same bleeding rate in every patient.
The negative control is established on a cohort member in the sibling study rather than re-run for all 21 patients; a cohort-wide no-bleed sweep is a proposed follow-up.
Acceptance rests on the deterministic pilot, not external literature (none was provided), so the bands are regression checks, not a population validation.

controls.name: no-bleed
controls.hypothesis: With no hemorrhage a patient loses no blood and vitals stay at their loaded values, confirming the cohort's loss and compensation come from the bleed and not from loading the state.
controls.expected: Under 1 mL lost; MAP and heart rate within 1 unit of their start.
controls.observed: Established on this engine for StandardMale (a cohort member) in the sibling hemorrhage-severity-sweep study, severity-0.0 arm — 0 mL lost, MAP 95.3 -> 95.3, heart rate 72.0 -> 71.2. A cohort-wide no-bleed sweep is a proposed follow-up.

controls.name: ExtremeFemale
controls.hypothesis: The smallest-volume patient, the extreme of the predictor, shows the bleed-and-compensate response and sits at the high-fraction end of the trend.
controls.expected: A clear bleed with compensation, and one of the largest fractions lost.
controls.observed: 1094 mL lost on a 2915 mL starting volume (~37.5%), near the top of the fraction range; blood volume and MAP fell and heart rate rose.

claim: All 21 shipped patients bleed and compensate the same way, and the fraction of blood lost falls with starting blood volume (Spearman rho = -0.89).

findings.statement: In every patient blood volume and MAP fell and heart rate rose. MAP fell by 3.8 mmHg (Bradycardic) to 32.2 mmHg (Joel); heart rate rose by 21.5 (Bradycardic) to 48.9 per min (Rick). No patient reached an irreversible state.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-23 at commit 5754940 (runs.db)

findings.statement: Absolute loss ranged from 1094 mL (ExtremeFemale) to 1755 mL (ExtremeMale), a much narrower spread than starting blood volume (2915 to 7095 mL), so the fraction lost ranged from 23.7% (Overweight) to 37.8% (Underweight); its Spearman rank correlation with starting blood volume is -0.89.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-23 at commit 5754940 (runs.db)

findings.statement: The fraction-volume trend follows from a shared compensation, not from different responses per patient. Every patient runs Pulse's same baroreflex (F-01), and the absolute loss is much less variable (1094-1755 mL) than the starting volume (2915-7095 mL); because a similar absolute loss is taken from very different reserves, the fraction lost falls as starting volume rises (rho = -0.89). The uniform mechanism, not patient-specific physiology, produces the correlation.

evidence.runs: canonical runs: investigation run of 2026-10-23 at commit 5754940 (runs.db)

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The fraction-volume correlation is driven by one or two outlier patients.
alternative_hypotheses.evidence: The correlation is Spearman (rank-based) over all 21 patients, rho = -0.89, which is not set by a single extreme value.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Larger patients lose a larger fraction, or there is no relationship.
alternative_hypotheses.evidence: The rank correlation is strongly negative (-0.89); smaller patients lose the larger fraction (F-02).

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Some patients do not compensate (a qualitatively different response).
alternative_hypotheses.evidence: F-01 — all 21 patients bled, lost volume and raised heart rate, and none reached an irreversible state.

discovery_implications.resolved: Across Pulse's 21 shipped patients the bleed-and-compensate response is qualitatively uniform, and the fraction lost falls with starting blood volume.
discovery_implications.remaining: Whether this holds for a real population rather than Pulse's shipped examples, and whether one severity means the same bleeding rate across body sizes.

followup_study_proposals.title: cohort-no-bleed-control
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Run the no-bleed arm for all 21 patients so the negative control is cohort-wide rather than borrowed from the StandardMale sibling run.

followup_study_proposals.title: severity-calibrated-to-flow
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Map Pulse severity to a per-patient flow rate so equal severity means equal bleeding rate, isolating body size from bleed rate.

conclusion:
## Claims
The hypothesis holds (23/23 tests passed).

## Limitations
The shipped patients are examples, not a population, and the same severity is not the same bleeding rate in every patient.
